newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries lower as market awaits Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries lower as market awaits Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices were lower Tuesday morning as market participants nervously awaited comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The 30-year Treasury bond was trading 10/32 lower at 95-16/32 to yield 6.86 percent.
Greenspan addresses the Senate Budget Committee at 1000 EST/1500 GMT and the market will closely monitor his remarks.
Also weighing on sentiment was an article in New York Times saying a tightening of monetary policy was unlikely in February but policymakers are ready to move should inflation surface.

"There was a little bit of pressure from the overnight session in Europe. There was a strong IFO -- a report on business conditions in Germany," said Kathy Bostjancic, economist at UBS securities. "If the data is really strong, it quells expectations of further easing by the Bundesbank."
That, in turn, creates negative sentiment for bonds in Europe, she said.

Offsetting that negative sentiment somewhat was a report that the British pound was fundamentally strong and that would lessen the need to move interest rates at this time, a positive development, Bostjancic said.
Bostjancic said there also was some trepidation ahead of Chairman Greenspan's comments.

Kevin Flanagan, economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc, said there was some apprehension about Greenspan's comments and also about the dollar coming off its high levels seen earlier in European sessions.
The dollar had hit a 42-month high against the yen before closing below the 118 level.
"The keys to Greenspan may not be his prepared text, but the types of questions he may get," Flanagan said. "The senators may ask him to expound on his 'irrational exuberance' comment."
Flanagan said trading activity should remain subdued until Greenspan speaks, but things could quickly get hectic.

"I think we're going to get a good idea of where all this is going early on. We have been seeing what are perceived as fairly hawkish comments coming from policymakers -- (who are) viewed as somewhat neutral -- lately," Flanagan said.
If Greenspan is seen as mirroring those views, the market may head lower fast, he said.
The Treasury will auction three- and six-month bills this afternoon. Federal funds were trading at 5.25 percent, right at the Fed's current target level.
Two-year notes were down 2/32 to 99-17/32, yielding 6.01 percent. Five-year notes were down 4/32 to 99-3/32, yielding 6.34 percent. Ten-year notes were down 6/32 to 99-14/32, yielding 6.58 percent.
Three-month bill rates were up one basis point to 5.03 percent. Six-month rates were up 2/32 at 5.09 percent and year bill rates were up two basis points to 5.31 percent.
